source_file_in_repo: GE Error Message Tool/source/Error Message Tool.html

field_notes.code: Ermes error number exactly as listed in the tool (anchor BM<code>).
field_notes.full_code/prefix: The tool lists bare Ermes numbers only; no "<prefix>:" form (e.g. 75004:) exists in the HTML or the PDF, so full_code == code and prefix is null. The app matches "<prefix>:<code>" queries by searching the part after the colon.
field_notes.code_block: Thousand-block used to split the HTML pages (not a GE category).
field_notes.symbol_group: Second token of the EM_ symbol (e.g. DIAG, RF, GP); derived, not a GE field.
field_notes.message: Error message text; hard line wraps joined, breaks kept before list items, "Label: %s" fields and after a trailing colon.
field_notes.extended_error: Extended Error text, unwrapped the same way. Verbatim wording.
field_notes.steps: extended_error split in order: list items (a), 1.) whole, other lines by sentence. Derived for display; extended_error is authoritative.
field_notes.frus: Possible cause(s), in tool order (most to least probable).
field_notes.fru_refs: Original GE service-desktop hrefs for linked FRUs (dead outside the scanner).
field_notes.documents: Document links in 2 entries (GE eServDocs, dead outside the scanner).
field_notes.system/subsystem/software_version: Not present in the tool; always null.
field_notes.pdf_cross_check_page: Page in error-codes-2247373.pdf where the code starts.

Protected image startup of the XG2 (XPS-PC2 X axis) failed. Check EMO reset and perform a TPS reset. If this error occurs again, contact your service representative.
entries.extended_error:
The XPS-PC2 inside X axis XPS failed to boot into protected mode.
* Verify that the X axis XPS and entire XG2 gradient subsystem is powered on.
* Verify that emergency stop is not active.
* Verify that the X axis dual-fiber cable is connected and properly seated into the IXG SFP transceiver module and X axis XPS.
* Verify X axis dual fiber optic cable linkup status and that there are no communication faults pertaining to the SFP transceiver modules in X axis XPS or in corresponding communications port on IXG board. SFP modules can be swapped between units for troubleshooting.
* Verify that both ends of the X axis XPS SFP Fiber cable are not damaged.
* Check the X axis XPS Heartbeat LED from the front panel is blinking.
* If Heartbeat LED not blinking then check condition of PDU 48V PS2 power supply.
* Power down the XG2 subsystem and reseat cables to X axis XPS. If these steps do not resolve the problem, replace the X axis XPS and perform a TPS reset.

entries.message: The %b XPS is reporting an Octavius power warning
entries.extended_error: Ensure the Octavius2 cable is not damaged and is properly connected between the XPS and XGA and reseat the cable. To verify cable is working properly, swap Octavius cables and perform a TPS reset (Note: swapping the cable will change the axis ID of the module). If the fault continues to be reported on the same axis ID after a TPS reset, replace the Ocativus cable. If the fault is reported on a new axis ID after a TPS reset, replace the XPS with the Ocativus cable ID reporting the issue.

entries.message: The %b XPS is reporting an Octavius Loss Of Signal Fault on the XGA.
entries.extended_error:
Ensure that the Octavius cable is connected properly to the XPS and XGA and the dual-fiber optic cable is properly connected between XGA and IXG. If error persists after a power cycle and TPS reset, swap Octavius cables and perform a TPS reset (Note:
swapping the cable will change the axis ID of the module). If the error is reported on the same axis ID, replace the octavius cable. If the error is reported on a new axis ID, swap SFP transceivers and perform a TPS reset. If error persists on the same axis, replace the XPS with the cable ID of the reported axis. If the error is reported on a new axis ID, replace the SFP transceiver.

entries.message: The IXG is reporting %b AC2 Axis2G link is down
entries.extended_error:
The following troubleshooting techniques can be used:
- Swap SFP transceivers between XGA units and perform a TPS reset. If error message is reported on a new axis, replace the SFP.
- Swap SFP transceivers between two XGA channels on the IXG side of the link and perform a TPS reset. If the error message is reported on a new axis, replace the SFP.
- Unplug dual-fiber cable on each side of the link, one side at a time and verify there is light. If no light is present on the transmit side of the cbale, replace the cable.
- Cycle gradient power and perform a TPS reset. If the error persists, replace the XGA.

entries.message: All of the power supply and amplifier Axis2G links are down, perform a TPS reset.
entries.extended_error:
- Check the 48V circuit breaker for 48V power and press the EMO reset button.
- Check the 48V power supply, verify the 48V power cables are properly connected.
- Check that all the dual-fiber cables are connected between the IXG and the XGA and XPS units.
- Check the LEDs on the XGA and XPS units, if none of the LEDs are lit, check teh 48V power supply in the PDU.

entries.message: The PC2 and AC2 %b Axis2G links are down on a single axis.
entries.extended_error: Check the Axis2G link LEDs on the IXG. If fault LEDs are displayed for both the XPS and XGA of the same axis, check the 48V power on the XPS and XGA by checking the front panel LEDs. If all LEDs are off, there is no power to the XPS and XGA. If the XPS and XGA have no power, check that the 48V power cable is connected from the PDU to the XPS and from the XPS to the XGA. If the front panel LEDs of the XPS and XGA are lit, check the dual-fiber cables and SFP modules at the XPS/XGA and the IXG. Dual-fiber cables and transceiver modules may be swapped to try and isolate the failure.
steps: Check the Axis2G link LEDs on the IXG.

entries.message: MPI network startup failed. Please perform System Restart.

There can be many reasons for this to occur such as network problems, faulty ICNs etc.

entries.message: An executable file necessary to run image reconstruction cannot be copied (path %s).
entries.extended_error: During TPS Reset the VRE ICNs will attempt to somtimes copy binary executables from the host. If this fails it is possible that those executables have been deleted or a network or NFS problem is preventing the ICN to pull the file from the host. It is also possible that the executable is still running on the machine and can therefore not be overridden. If this problem presists a software reload may be required.

entries.message: Unable to reset VRE, will try to recover before failing TPS Reset.
entries.extended_error: Internally the VRE reset code has the ability to detect problems and attempt to correct them. This usually means rebooting the VRE. Other operator level messages are logged to inform the operator that the TPS Reset will take longer than normal.
steps: Internally the VRE reset code has the ability to detect problems and attempt to correct them.

entries.message: Failed to reset the VRE. All attempts to recover have failed. Try performing a System Restart and call Service on repeated occurrence.
entries.extended_error: During TPS Reset we also reset the VRE (and all its ICNs). This failure means that we could not recover the VRE. Scanning won't be possible. Most likely there is a problem with one or more ICNs and their connection to the host. Seeing this message also means that fail-over (i.e. running the VRE with a reduced set of ICNs) wasn't possible. A host reboot may potentially fix this problem. Troubleshoot VRE subsystem.

entries.message: VRE configuration changes detected. Do you want the system to accept these changes? Selecting OK means that the VRE will potentially run in degraded mode (which reduces image reconstruction performance) and the System needs to be restarted.
entries.extended_error: This message is displayed to the operator in form of a popup at the beginning on the TPS Reset. Seeing this means that the VRE configuration has been changed, which could mean that ICNs were disabled, enabled, added, removed etc. A System Restart will be necessary for those changes to take affect, therefore the current TPS Reset will fail if OK is selected. Selecting CANCEL will undo all VRE configuration changes and attempt to reset with the current configuration.

entries.message: VRE configuration changes detected. Cannot accept the current VRE configuration changes as image reconstruction could no longer be performed. The current TPS Reset will fail, please notify Service.
entries.extended_error: This message is displayed to the operator in form of a popup at the beginning or end of the TPS Reset. Seeing this means that the VRE configuration has been changed but in a way that makes it impossible to scan. This could happen either because there are no ICNs left in the configuration or because those ICNs left are missing features necessary for scanning, such as acquisition hardware or Infiniband connections.

entries.message: The VRE is running in degraded mode, which means that image reconstruction will be slower than normal. Please make sure Service is notified.
entries.extended_error: This message is displayed to the operator in form of a popup during a TPS Reset to remind him that we're running the VRE in degraded mode. This means that one or more ICNs have been disabled either because they caused TPS Reset failures and thus were removed automatically or because they were disabled manually by Service. The customer can keep scanning but the faulty ICN(s) should be replaced as quickly as possible to restore full recon performance.

entries.extended_error: The MGD failed to start a TPS Reset. Either the serial connection to the MGD STIF Board is not working or the Ethernet connection from the Host to the MGD Hub is not working. Run the APS, AGP, and SCP Host Data path ping tests to check the Ethernet connections. Run the APS, AGP, and SCP Board Level Diagnostics to check the SCSI Serial Expansion. The STIF Board serial connection is not tested. If both sets of diagnostics pass but yet the TPS Reset still fails then please closely inspect the serial connection between the SCSI Serial Expansion and the MGD STIF Board. APS, AGP, and SCP Board Level Diagnostics included. VRE failure can sometimes trigger the failure of MGD boards. Failure of SCP with APS/AGP board can be a indicator on the failure on respective board. On APS,SCP,AGP failure run the Board Level Diagnostics to conform the status.

entries.message:
TPS Reset Communication Failure:
Host to %s board ethernet communication timed out during TPS Reset.
entries.extended_error:
Verify the following to determine the cause of this failure:
Check that the MGD Chassis is turned on and power supplies are OK.
Check that the board is properly seated, there are no bent pins on the backplane slot for the board, and the board has power.
Check that the ethernet connection to the board is present.
Check that the term server to STIF board reset cable connection is good and that the term server power and ethernet connection is good.

entries.extended_error:
The SRI detected that the cradle moved at a velocity different than what was commanded. This message is expected to be logged when the operator moves the cradle by hand.
Do not troubleshoot based on this error alone. This issue should only be investigated if the site reports the cradle stopping before it gets to the desired position along with this message being logged.
To investigate, run the table motion diagnostic.
If the commanded and measured velocity are both in the same direction (both positive or both negative) and the measured velocity is less than the expected velocity, then there could be a table obstruction preventing the cradle from moving fast enough. Check the cradle and trolley for friction points to the table and bridge. Make sure the belt has proper motion.
If the previous checks pass, make sure that the encoder shielding is intact and that the encoder to SRI cable shielding is intact. If the encoder is OK, check the long drive motor, the SSM or PHPS, and the SRI.

entries.extended_error:
If this problem occurs, it is probably intermittent. This will be a difficult problem to diagnose.
If this error occurs, then the GAP, MIF, and cables between the two are suspect. Swapping MIF Modules is a possibility so that the error can be tracked to see if it moves. If the problem moves, then the MIF Module is the problem. Cables can also be swapped. However, the GAP is a single item in the system, and cannot be swapped. Currently, there are no diagnostics or tests to find this problem.

Hardware Error - No Gradient Clock.\b\ A gradient clock stop occurred. The GAP stopped receiving the gradient clock from the IPG. Check the connection between the TYME Board and the GAP Board, then run fiber optic diagnostics.
entries.extended_error: This error condition can also be caused by the Gradient Data Clock Fiber Optic Cables or HSSD Cables being located in the wrong position . In addition to generating this error, if the Gradient Data Clock is not correctly connected, then the system will not go Ready either. Also, if this error seems to be intermittent, and you are getting many other errors, and you have been Resetting TPS, or running Gradient Driver Tests, then, it is possible that IPG could not report all of the tests that have been generated. If this is the case, check the Gradient Data Cable connections to ensure that all, including the Gradient Clock, are in the correct location. When the errors come back from these tests, then check the last line in the error message that reads Low: XXXv High: XXXv Value: 0V axis: XXXXXXX" Notice that if all the error messages that read values are coming back with a value of 0v, or 0mV, then this is an indication the Gradient Clock may be missing.This could also indicate a power problem somewhere in this subsystem. check for things that are common to the axis that are failing."

entries.extended_error: To make sure that you are not looking at faulty sensing from the ASM Board, try swapping the ASM Board for the axis with the fault with an ASM Board from another axis to see if the problem changes axis. If the problem changes axis, then the ASM Board is bad. Remember to use proper ESD practices when changing these boards. If the ASM's are OK, and this is a system with a GRAM, then there is probably a GRAM current distortion error and/or an analog saturation error. If this error occurs during GRAM Tuning, then the VBUS (Bus Voltage Regulator) may not be set up correctly.(This calibration is in the GRAM Tuning procedure.) Adjust this parameter per the GRAM Tuning Calibration, and try again.

entries.extended_error: If you have been using an oscilloscope, or performing GRAM Tuning, it may be possible that you did not use power from the Filtered Service Outlet. It is critical to use this filtered outlet because noise from other sources of power can feed from the scope back into the GRAM Control Board causing calibrations and measurements to be extremely inaccurate. It is possible to get this error if this kind of noise has been introduced into the GRAM. If your oscilloscope uses a voltage other than the 120VAC from the Service Outlet, then try using a step up transformer plugged into this filtered service outlet. In this way, you have the advantage of the filtered service outlet at the correct voltage for your oscilloscope.

GRADIENT CONFIGURATION ERROR.\b\ The MRconfig.cfg file indicates a X axis GRAM is present, but the DIP switch on the front of the MIF is not set. The GAP software is not controlling the GRAM, but analog Vin and voltage control are set in GRAM mode.
entries.extended_error: If the MRConfig.cfg file has been changed, a Reset TPS MUST be performed. After a Reset TPS, SPI will check the MRconfig.cfg file to compare the software configuration of with the hardware settings. If the hardware differs from the MRconfig.cfg file, SPI will log an error, and will not allow the Gradient Driver Subsystem to go Ready. Swap the ASM Board for the axis with the fault with an ASM Board from another axis to see if the problem changes axis. If the problem changes axis, then the ASM Board is bad. If the problem stays on the same axis, try swapping the GASM Board for the axis with the fault with a GASM Board from another axis to see if the problem changes axis. If the problem changes axis, then the GASM Board is bad. Remember to use proper ESD practices when changing these boards.

Analogic RF Amplifier Cable Fault. The RF Interface (RFI) is reporting the cable is disconnected or defective between the RFI and the Analogic RF Amplifier.
Analogic RF Amplifier Power Loss Fault. RF Interface (RFI) detects no power to Analogic RF Amplifier. Possible cause: the breaker on the front of the RFI is turned off.

Analogic RF Amplifier Power Supply Fault. Analogic RF Amplifier indicates the main power supply is out of specification. Possible causes: Supply feedback loop exceeds specification, PS heat sink is overheated, Power supply FETS are shorted.
Analogic RF Amplifier Duty Cycle Fault. Unblank duty cycle exceeds specification.
Analogic RF Amplifier I Peak Overloaded Fault. Instantaneous peak drain current of RF devices exceeds specification.
Analogic RF Amplifier Device Fault 44. RF FET device is shorted. Replace amplifier.
Analogic RF Amplifier High Voltage Low Fault. Analogic RF Amplifier power supply voltage dropped below specification.
Analogic RF Amplifier High Voltage High Fault. Analogic RF Amplifier power supply voltage went above specification.

Analogic RF Amplifier Excessive Input Drive Fault. Analogic RF Amplifier detects input greater than specification. Possible causes: RF Interface (RFI) miscalibration, defective exciter, or defective RF Amplifier.

Analogic RF Amplifier Overheat Fault. Analogic RF Ampl reports the thermal switch has exceeded 80 C. Possible causes: restricted air flow, blown fan fuse, defective fan, room environment out of specification or defective RF Amplifier.

Analogic RF Amplifier Peak Power Fault. Peak power from Analogic RF Amplifier exceeds specification. Possible causes: RF Interface (RFI) calibration, defective RFI output stage, defective Exciter or defective RF Amplifier.

Analogic RF Amplifier Average Power Fault. Analogic RF Amp reports its average power has exceeded specification. Possible causes: the PSD is exceeding the limits of the system, defective RF Interface (RFI) output stage, or defective RF Amp.

Analogic RF Amplifier Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) Fault. Analogic RF Amp reflected power exceeds specification. Possible causes: disconnected or defective output cable from RF Amplifier to RF Interface (RFI), defective RFI or RF Amp.

Analogic RF Amplifier Gate Fault. Analogic RF Amp reports an unblank pulse width exceeding specification. Possible causes: the PSD is exceeding the limits of the system, defective RF Interface (RFI) or defective RF Amplifier.
Analogic RF Amplifier Junction Temp Fault. Analogic RF Amplifier device junction temperature is greater than specification.

entries.extended_error: To make sure that you are not looking at faulty sensing from the ASM Board, try swapping the ASM Board for the axis with the fault with an ASM Board from another axis to see if the problem changes axis. If the problem changes axis, then the ASM Board is bad. Remember to use proper ESD practices when changing these boards. This error condition can also be caused by the Gradient HSSD Cables being located in the wrong position. In addition to generating this error, if the Gradient Data Clock is not correctly connected, then the system will not go Ready. One way to check the Gradient Data Clock connections is to check the last line of the error messages. If it reads Low: XXXv High: XXXv Value: 0V axis: XXXXXXX", then this is an indication the Gradient Clock may be missing. This could also indicate a power problem somewhere in the subsystem. Check for things that are common to the axes that are failing."

GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - Static Test MIF %c Axis Configuration Error. Required: Current Sum=0, Low-side Invert=1, Serv Mode=0, Manual Ena=0. Current: Current Sum=%d, Low-side Invert=%d, Serv Mode=%d, Manual Ena=%d. No tests will be run on this axis.
entries.extended_error: Current Sum configuration error could cause this fault. Move the DIP switch (S1) on the MIF Circuit Board to the Current Sum true position. Low side inverter configuration error could also cause this fault. Move the DIP switch (S2) on the MIF Circuit Board to the Low Side Polarity true position. Service mode is the logic OR of switches S4-1 through S4-5 (these are the DIP switches on the MIF front panel)...the first five dip switches must be set in the up configuration. Your system should not be in the Manual Enable mode...it must be in GAP control...S3, the three position slide switch should be all the way to the right (series switch can be down) After a Reset TPS, SPI will check the MRconfig.cfg file to compare the software configuration of with the hardware settings. If the hardware differs from the MRconfig.cfg file, SPI will log an error, and will not allow the Gradient Driver Subsystem to go Ready. If all switches are correct, and the problem still exists, then swap the MIF chassis of the axis with the fault with a MIF chassis of another axis, and re-run this test.

If the problem remains on the same axis, use the GRAM Troubleshooting Harness, 2141174, to swap the GRAM Module to confirm the functionality of the GRAM Module or Status and Control Cables. If the problem changes axis, then the GRAM Module or Status and Control Cables internal to the GRAM Cabinet are bad for that axis. If the problem remains on the same axis, then the cables external to the GRAM Cabinet are bad. If the hardware differs from the MRconfig.cfg file, SPI will log an error, and will not allow the Gradient Driver Subsystem to go Ready.

entries.extended_error: For GRAM Service Mode, Inverter Ready should be a 1 and displayed as green on DS, within 15 seconds of a power cycle. Control Ready should be a 1 and displayed as green at all times, unless power is turned off. If Inverter Ready and Control Ready conditions are not correct, replace the GRAM for that axis. The four position dip switch on the GRAM Control Board should all be in the inactive, or 0, position.S1 should be in the Enable (Up) position. If Inverter Ready and Control Ready conditions are not correct, replace the GRAM for that axis. If the MRConfig.cfg file has been changed, a Reset TPS MUST be performed. After a Reset TPS, SPI will check the MRconfig.cfg file to compare the software configuration of with the hardware settings. If the hardware differs from the MRconfig.cfg file, SPI will log an error, and will not allow the Gradient Driver Subsystem to go Ready.

entries.extended_error: If the system is a Signa Horizon, there would be no current output. The image would look like a flat image. If the system has a GRAM, then an error message would have indicated a fault, and the scanner would not be permitted to go to Ready. If there was a G in the ipg_stage file, and you performed a scan, the output voltage would be proportional to the DAC signal. This will generate too much voltage and an I Overcurrent and I Distorition fault will occur. If too much current is generated, then there will be an overload condition. In either case, replace the MIF Module.
steps: If the system is a Signa Horizon, there would be no current output.
The image would look like a flat image.
If the system has a GRAM, then an error message would have indicated a fault, and the scanner would not be permitted to go to Ready.
If there was a G in the ipg_stage file, and you performed a scan, the output voltage would be proportional to the DAC signal.
This will generate too much voltage and an I Overcurrent and I Distorition fault will occur.
If too much current is generated, then there will be an overload condition.
In either case, replace the MIF Module.

This test result indicates that the MIF Module must be replaced. If the system has a GRAM, the system would have generated Power Module overloads. The MIF Module must be replaced.

entries.extended_error: If power is applied to the GRAM, and the DIP switch is in the no GRAM position, and you are trying to troubleshoot by bypassing the GRAM, then, the GRAM has to be taken out of the circuit. The GRAM has to be wired out of the circuit, not just turned off when bypassing the GRAM. If there is no GRAM, but software detects that there is a GRAM, then the DIP switch is not being read properly, this is probably a bad MIF Module. Try toggling the dip switch and re-run this test. If the problem goes away, then the dip switch is probably failing intermittently. Replace the MIF Module. If the problem does not go away, then try swapping the MIF Module and re- running the test. If the problem moves, replace the MIF Module. If the problem stays on the same axis, then there is probably a cable problem. Re-check the cable connections and run numbers.

entries.extended_error:
The following conditions can cause this ERROR:
a) >140A average current (OCAVG LED DS7)
b) >275A peak current (OCINST LED DS8)
c) >80% Pulse Width Modulation (OCDUTY LED DS6)
d) >800,000 Amp transitions/sec (OCDUTY LED DS6) If this condition, suspect the PSD. Remove the JP1 located on miniGRAM control Board to latch the appropriate LED. If this error occurs 4 more times, 2241548 will be reported and you will have to cycle power to the GRAM Power Supply to reset it.

entries.message: GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - %c Axis Fault Occurred. The GIP reported a %c Axis miniGRAM OverVoltage Fault. Try swapping the miniGRAM Control Board, or the entire miniGRAM axis, or the miniGRAM Power Supply to isolate the problem. %b
entries.extended_error: This occurs if miniGRAM Power Supply voltage is > 850 VDC. If error follows miniGRAM, swap miniGRAM Control Boards to further isolate cause and replace the defective component. If this error occurs 4 more times, 2241547 will be reported and you will have to cycle power to the GRAM Power Supply to reset it.

entries.message: GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - %c Axis Fault Occurred. The GIP reported a Transistor Fault on the %c Axis of the GPM. This fault could be related to noise. Possible causes: Cable between the GIP and GPM, Axis GPM Main Board or Output Shelf. %b
entries.extended_error: If the transistor fault happens immediately when the scanner goes to Ready, this indicates a shorted transistor and the Output Shelf for this axis will have to be replaced. If this error occurs 4 more times, 2241546 will be reported and you will have to cycle power to the GPM Power Supply to reset it. If the fault is intermittent, swap the GPM Main Board for the failing axis with another Main Board to isolate the cause of the fault to the Main Board or the Output Shelf. Replace the component that reproduces the fault.

entries.message: GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - Fault Occurred. The GIP reported a GPM Power Supply Fault. Check the GPM or the GPM Power Supply. %b
entries.extended_error: This error can be caused by Overtemp, Overcurrent, or Overvoltage conditions on GPM Power Supply. If the error occurs 4 more times, error 2241550 will be generated and power to the GPM Power Supply will need to be cycled to reset it. If error sequence reoccurs then remove output cables from the back of the GPM one at a time to isolate to GPM axis (you must always have at least one output connected or a Power Supply fault will occur.). Note: while running with an output disconnected from an axis, you can ignore error 2241522 or 2242045 for that axis.

entries.message: DMA API - Close operation failed because the HPI interface, used for DMA transfers to 16 bit memory, could not be successfully closed.
entries.extended_error: DMA transfers to 16 bit memory require transfers to 32 bit Fast Update and 32 bit Burst memory. On-board hardware decode logic detects write transactions to Fast Update and Burst memory, and then initiate write transactions to 16 bit memory through the HPI interface. To ensure exclusive access to HPI hardware, software interfaces are used. During plcDmaSetup(), an HPI interface is opened (reserved for exclusive use) when the destination DMA location is Fast Update or Burst memory. The HPI interface is stored in the DMA interface handle. When the DMA interface is closed using plxDmaClose(), the HPI handle is closed. This error occurred because HPI close operation failed. Either (1) the HPI API environment is corrupted, or (2) the DMA interface handle is corrupted.

entries.extended_error: BOARD_TYPE, which is the second parameter of plxDmaOpen(), is the enumerated value that defines which board is responsible for performing the DMA transfer. This parameter is a valid BOARD_TYPE value. However, the DMA API initializes a board definitions table, gstrBoardDefs[] (indexed by BOARD_TYPE), that defines various board parameters related to performing DMA transfers. The table element bDmaResident is based on an element bDmaIsResident in the static table gstrBoardTypeInfo[] (defined in dmaSys.c). This element indicates the board specified in the open operation does not support DMA transfers - meaning a DMA controller is not resident.

entries.message: DMA API - Setup HPI operation failed because the HPI interface was already opened by a previous DMA setup or setup HPI function operation.
entries.extended_error:
HPI hardware, which provides access to 16 bit memory resident on custom boards, is controlled by a software interface that ensures exclusive access. The HPI interface is used by the DMA API and other software, but can also be shared provided the 'other' software supervises the shared HPI interface. If the DMA API controls (is responsible for opening/closing the HPI interface), the HPI interface, call sequence is plxDmaOpen(), then plxDmaSetup(). If the 'supervisory' software will control the HPI interface, the call sequence is:
plxDmaOpen(), plxDmaSetupHpi(), then plxDmaSetup(). If the HPI interface handle is not defined when plxDmaSetup() is called for the first time, the DMA API takes control of the HPI interface. Otherwise, the DMA API assumes the calling software is supervising the HPI which had to be communicated using the plxDmaSetupHpi() function. This error is a result of plxDmaSetupHpi() being called when the HPI interface handle stored in the DMA interface handle already exists. Either (1) the DMA interface handle is corrupted, (2) plxDmaSetupHpi() was called mulitple times, or
(3) plxDmaSetupHpi() was called after plxDmaSetup().

entries.message: DMA API - Open operation failed because the DMA semaphore name, which is based off the board & channel parameters, was not found by the O/S function, smNameFind(), in the sempahore database.
entries.extended_error:
The DMA API is initialized when plxDmaOpen() is called for the first time. The state of the system is examined, global tables are built, and sempahores are created. For each board capable of performing DMA transfers, semaphore entries consisting of an ID and name are created for each of the DMA controller's channels. The semaphore name is a string based on the board and channel. During the open operation, the semaphore database is accessed, searching for the semaphore name that is based off the plxDmaopen() parameters. The smNameFind() function could not find the semaphore name in the database. Either (1) the board & channel is not a valid DMA API interface, (2) the semaphore database was corrupted, or
(3) the semaphore name was inadvertently removed from the database.

entries.extended_error:
Once the DMA transfer is initiated, a semTake() function call attempts to take a blocking semaphore that is not available until the DMA ISR handler frees the blocking semaphore. The second parameter in the semTake() function specifies the duration to wait for the blocking semaphore to become available. The following conditions may exist:
(1) A lengthy DMA transfer did not complete in the timeframe allotted. The timeout parameter should be increased. (2) The ISR handler was not called because of a hardware or O/S error. After the timeout occurred, software attempted to clean up the hardware by aborting the DMA transfer. The cleanup was successful.

entries.message: A broadband Exciter1A was found in the master exciter slot of the RRF chassis. This might degrade image quality. Normally, only the Exciter2 is used as a master and Exciter1A is optionally used as a slave.

entries.message: ONLY 16 OF 32 RF RECEIVER CHANNELS PRESENT This system is configured for 32 RF Receiver channels but some or all of the channels in the 2nd RRF chassis are not responding. 32 channel scans will not be possible. 8 or 16 channel scans should work.
entries.extended_error:
Check the GB0 - GB3 LEDs on the IRF board in the MGD chassis. For a 32 channel system, they all should be on. The GB0 LED is for RRF channels 1-8 which is the fiber on the IRFIO board that MUST be connected to the master DIF board in the 1st RRF chassis. The GB1-3 LEDs are for the fiber connectors on the front edge of the IRF2 board. Those three fibers can be connected in any order but a 32ch system expects to see all three fibers connected and active. This system does not see a connection to one or both DIFs in the 2nd RRF chassis.
Make sure that the option key configuration matches the hardware configuration. If this system does not have the hardware installed that is needed for 32 channel scans, the 32 channel option key should not be installed.

entries.message: WARNING: An 20MHz DRF2 board is installed in this system. This is a prototype board that must be replaced with a 40MHz production version of the DRF2 board.
This system does not have a master exciter in the 1st RRF chassis that is compatible with 32 channel scans. The system requires an exciter that can drive a clock signal to the 2nd master exciter.
entries.extended_error: A 32 channel system requires a special master exciter in both RRF chassis. These exciters have an inter-connect cable that allows both exciters to run from the same clock source. The system detected an exciter that does not have this capability. Without this type of exciter, 32-channel scans may be corrupted because the two RRF chassis are not clock synchronized. If this system is not intended to run 32 channel scans, remove the 32 channel option key.

entries.extended_error: Sys Cab and UTNS Bypass Diag: Dead channels while running these diags indicate a problem with a board in the receive chain (MUX, UTNS, Rx), or cables between the boards. Sixteen bad channels (or eight bad channels in an eight channel system would indicate a problem with the signal source, or problems other than the three receive chain boards. Eight bad channels in a 16 channel system would indicate a bad board. Swapping good boards with suspected boards is an effective way to isolate a problem. Problems with banks of channels (1-4, 5-8, etc) may indicate a problem with a receive When individual bad channels (1,8,9,16) may lead to an improperly seated cable.\n 16 Channel Switch diag: If problems exist when running this diagnostic, the Sys Cab Loopback diag should also be performed. If the Sys Cab loopback test fails too, then there is a likely problem inside the system cabinet. If the Sys Cab Loopback diag passes, there is probably a problem between the Mux and the 16 Channel Switch(inclusive). For the 16 Channel Switch results, a failure of all 16 channels would indicate a problem with the switch itself. The ports or hte oscillators could be bad. To test the oscillators, try running the Multi-Coil Receive II Diagnostic. For 8 channel failures, check the switch, corresponding ports, or specific cables. Look for trends in the failures for the various port tests.\n Multi-Coil Receive II Diagnostic: To isolate problems between the LPCA connectors and the 16 Channel Switch, the Sys Cab and 16 Channel Switch Diags should be executed first. In conjunction with those results, conclusions may be drawn as to whether the problem resides in the signals' paths.

entries.message:
ADC offsets calibration validation failed. The acquired ADC offsets are out of tolerance for the following receivers.
Rx=%s%s%s%s%s%s%s%s%s A TPS reset may be necessary.
entries.extended_error:
Probable causes for this failure:
1) The software state of the system. The software failed to set a Remote RF value properly, which led to improper data acquisition. A TPS reset can solve software related issues. If the error recurs after a reset, then a hardware problem is more likely.
2) The hardware is causing problems. Repeatable problems may be due to a board failure. There are basically three regions to examine. First, the Exciter may be bad, which would indicate consistently bad results across all channels. Second, the receive data chain within the RRF chassis could be bad. Run MGD Board Level and MGD Data Path diagnostics and then run RRF Board Level and Data Path Diagnostics. If the problem appears to be due to low receive signal on one or more channels then run the RRF Receive Chain FRU Isolation Diagnostic to identify the failing MUX, UTNS3, Receiver, or RRF-DIF Board.

RRF Serial Number registers not loaded. Presence and validation of Remote RF boards could not be confirmed. Valid status memory reads - %d
entries.extended_error: For each of the Remote RF boards, serial number status memory registers are not available until 7-9 microseconds following reset. The RRF-DIF Status register contains a status bit, Serial Number Loaded from ROM, which indicates the validity of the serial number registers. This bit was polled several times. For each iteration, the status bit is checked to confirm serial number registers were successfully loaded. If valid, polling stops. Otherwise, a WriteWait() call is made in order to allow status memory to be updated for the next polling attempt. If the number of valid status memory reads is 0, status memory is not getting updated.

For each iteration, the status bit is checked to confirm serial number registers were successfully loaded.
If valid, polling stops.
Otherwise, a WriteWait() call is made in order to allow status memory to be updated for the next polling attempt.
If the number of valid status memory reads is 0, status memory is not getting updated.

entries.message: SCIM Communication Error. The keyboard serial port reported an error upon reception of a character. Serial status: 0x%02X Character: 0x%02X
entries.extended_error:
The SCP serial port that communicates to the SCIM reported a serial link error. This could be either a framing error or a receive overrun.
A framing error (Serial status: 0x10) indicates a timing problem on the serial link, which could be caused by an intermittent cable connection, faulty cable, or a faulty SCIM or SCP. This is most likely a cable problem.
An overrun error (Serial status: 0x02) indicates that the SCP could not keep up with the receive data coming from the SCIM. This is most likely a problem with the SCP.
This message might also occur if the power to the SCIM has been shut down while performing system maintenance or if the SCIM power is intermittent.
Check that the SCIM has power, which is supplied via the cable from the GOCAA/WIM.
Check that the communication link is connected between the STIF(or PSE) and the SCIM and that there are no loose connections.
Please run the keyboard (SCIM) diagnostics to locate the problem.

entries.message: RF Amplifier fault %02d.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault. Fault interlock held in the faulted state. Microprocessor is in reset, or possible defective cable between Processor Board and Display Board.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 01. Internal EPROM contents inconsistent with a run. The microprocessor detected a possible check-sum error Possible address bus fault or defective EPROM on the processor board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 02. Dual port RAM problem. Possible defective Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 03. A/D has failed. Possible problem with Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 04. A/D multiplexer has failed. Possible problem with the Processor Board or 1 of the 32 analog signals.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 05. A/D self-test in the microprocessor has failed. The check of the Gnd., 1/2 Vcc, and Vcc in the microprocessor failed. Possible defective Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 06. Stepping motor coil is open. Possible defective or open motor cable, open stepping motor winding, or defective Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 07. Illegal opcode. Possible defective Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 08. Microprocessor external interrupt high does not cause an interrupt. Possible defective Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 09. Microprocessor external interrupt low does not cause an interrupt. Possible defective Processor Board.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 10. Heat sink monitor temperature unacceptable. Possible defective thermistor on Solid State Amplifier Board or disconnected cable between Processor Board and Solid State Amplifier Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 11. SCM cable interlock fault. Possible disconnected or defective SCM Jumper Connector.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 12. 100V power supply unacceptable - less than 88V or greater than 147V. Possible defective Power Control Board, IPI or PA tube, or open cables.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 13. IPA HV unacceptable. +3kV power supply is below 2.25kV or more than 3.784kV; probably a low voltage. Possible defective IPA tube or bad High Voltage Rectifier/Filter Board. Check line voltage for low or varying voltage.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 14. IPA heater current unacceptable. The current is either greater than 1.9 amps or less than 1.1 amps. Possible defective IPA tube, Power Control Board, or harness.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 15. -5V power supply unacceptable. Less than -5.4V or greater than -4.2V. Possible defective Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 16. 48V power supply unacceptable. Less than 42.9V or greater than 51.5V. Possible defective Power Control Board or Solid State Amplifier Board.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 17. PA HV unacceptable. +6kV less than 4.5kV or greater than 7.592kV; most probably a low voltage. Possible defective PA tube or HV Rectifier/Filter Board. Check incoming power for low or varying voltages.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 18. PA heater current unacceptable. The current is either greater than 16 amps or less than 12 amps. Possible defective PA tube, Power Control Board, or harness.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 19. 32V power supply unacceptable, less than 21.8V or greater than 38.4V. Possible defective AC Switching Module connectors or fuses F3, F6, or F9. Check for excessive loading, such as on the stepping motors.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 20. 2.5V reference unacceptable. Less than 2.2V or greater than 2.7V. Possible defective Processor Board or AC Switching Module transformer T1 or fuses.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 21. 24V power supply unacceptable. Less than 22.3V or greater than 25V. Possible defective Power Control Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 22. Motor 1 zero fault. Either motor 1 is stuck at zero or AFT has failed and forced motor to zero. Possible defective motor or cable.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 23. Motor 2 zero fault. Either motor 2 is stuck at zero or AFT has failed and forced motor to zero. Possible defective motor or cable.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 24. Motor 3 zero fault. Either motor 3 is stuck at zero or AFT has failed and forced motor to zero. Possible defective motor or cable.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 25. Motor 4 zero fault. Either motor 4 is stuck at zero or AFT has failed and forced motor to zero. Possible defective motor or cable.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 26. Motor 1 zero not found, although the zero was found while initializing. Possible defective cables to motor 1 and zero sensors, and drivers on Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 27. Motor 2 zero not found, although the zero was found while initializing. Possible defective cables to motor 2 and zero sensors, and drivers on Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 28. Motor 3 zero not found, although the zero was found while initializing. Possible defective cables to motor 3 and zero sensors, and drivers on Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 29. Motor 4 zero not found, although the zero was found while initializing. Possible defective cables to motor 4 and zero sensors, and drivers on Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 30. Motor or washer stuck. All motors were able to pass the zero and non-zero tests during initialization. Now, one or more is not operating correctly.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 32. Unblank longer than 20 msec. The rising and falling edge of the unblank signal did not fall within the 20 msec time limit. Check the unblank cable and the Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 33. Unblank without Power Monitor.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 35. FET 1 coarse convergence failed. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board, Processor Board, or cables between them.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 36. FET 2 coarse convergence failed. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board, Processor Board, or cables between them.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 37. FET 3 coarse convergence failed. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board, Processor Board, or cables between them.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 38. FET 4 coarse convergence failed. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board, Processor Board, or cables between them.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 42. FET 1 fine convergence failed. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board, Processor Board, or cables between them.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 43. FET 2 fine convergence failed. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board, Processor Board, or cables between them.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 44. FET 3 fine convergence failed. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board, Processor Board, or cables between them.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 45. FET 4 fine convergence failed. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board, Processor Board, or cables between them.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 46. FET 1 bias tracked out of range. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board (most likely), Processor Board, or cables between them.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 47. FET 2 bias tracked out of range. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board (most likely), Processor Board, or cables between them.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 48. FET 3 bias tracked out of range. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board (most likely), Processor Board, or cables between them.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 49. FET 4 bias tracked out of range. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board (most likely), Processor Board, or cables between them.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 50. 100V power supply was less than 85V one second after 100V start relay closed. Possible defective Power Control Board, AC Switching Module, or excessive loading on power supply bus.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 51. 100V power supply was less than 90V one msec after 100V run relay closed. Possible defective Power Control Board, AC Switching Module, or excessive loading on power supply bus - possibly a PA tube heater.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 52. IPA heater current was unacceptable one second after heater relay was enabled. Possible defective IPA tube, Power Control Board, or harness between tube and Power Control Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 53. PA heater current was unacceptable. Current is less than 10.6 amps or greater than 18.6 amps. Possible defective Power Control Board, PA tubes, or harness.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 54. PA tube heater soft-start failure within 15 seconds. Possible defective PA tube, Power Control Board, or Processor Board.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 55. 3kV power supply unacceptable within 0.5 sec after closing HV start relay. Possible defective HV rectifier/filter board, bad relay in AC Switching Module, or bad A/D on Processor Board.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 56. +6kV power supply unacceptable within 0.5 sec after closing HV start relay. Possible defective HV rectifier/filter board, bad relay in AC Switching Module, or bad A/D on Processor Board.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 57. +3kV power supply unacceptable within 0.5 to 6 seconds after closing HV start relay. Possible defective HV rectifier/filter board, bad relay in AC Switching Module, or bad A/D on Processor Board.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 58. +6kV power supply unacceptable within 0.5 to 6 seconds after closing HV start relay. Possible defective HV rectifier/filter board, bad relay in AC Switching Module, or bad A/D on Processor Board.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 59. HV Rectifier/Filter Board unacceptable within 100msec of closing HV run relay. Possible defective HV rectifier/filter board, bad relay in AC Switching Module, or bad A/D on Processor Board.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 60. IPA tube AFT algorithm has gone beyond limit. The AFT routine could not converge after 160 steps of the IPA tune and load capacitors. Possible defective IPA phase detector board, motor drivers or A/D on processor board.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 61. PA tube AFT algorithm has gone beyond limit. The AFT routine could not converge after 800 steps of the PA tune and load capacitors. Possible defective PA phase detector board, motor drivers, or A/D on processor board.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 62. Insufficient power for AFT. Not enough power was seen at the IPA envelope detector to perform AFT. Possible defective Solid State Amplifier Board, bad connection to VTAC, bad IPA tube, input board or phase detector.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 70. Operate command fault. An invalid command was received by the microprocessor. Possible shorted SCM cable or defective Processor Board.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 71. Frequency command fault. Amp was commanded to the wrong frequency or frequency command was given while amp was in operate state. Possible cause: wrong magnet field strength in system config file (.5T vs 1.0T vs 1.5T)
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 72. Mode command fault. The mode command was given while the amplifier was in the operate state or the amplifier was commanded to an invalid mode.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 73. PA (Body mode) forward power too high. Possible defective Erbtec RF Monitor Module, or high input signal to the amp, or bad A/D on processor board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 74. IPA (Head mode) forward power too high. Possible defective Erbtec RF Monitor Module, or high input signal to the amp, or bad A/D on processor board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 75. PA (Body mode) reflected power too high. Possible disconnected output cable, or improper load outside of the amplifier, or bad A/D on processor board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 76. IPA (Head mode) reflected power too high. Possible disconnected output cable, or improper load outside of the amplifier, or bad A/D on processor board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 77. PA grid current too high. Possible defective PA tube, or problems on the power control board or processor board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 78. IPA grid current too high. Possible defective IPA tube, or problems on the power control board or processor board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 79. PA plate current too high. Possible defective PA tube, bad High Voltage Rectifier/Filter Board, Power Control Board, or Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 80. IPA plate current too high. Possible defective IPA tube, bad High Voltage Rectifier/Filter Board, Power Control Board, or Processor Board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 81. 3kV arc detected. Possible defective IPA tube or bad processor board.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 82. Cover interlock 1 on HV tube cavity side. Possible defective cover and switch.
ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 83. Cover interlock 2 on processor board side. Possible defective cover and switch.

ERBTEC RF Amplifier fault 84. RF power monitor fault. Proper signals are not being received from RF power monitor. Possible defective power monitor, cables, Processor Board, or power monitor microprocessor power momentarily dropped causing a reset.

RF Amplifier fault 85. RF Transmit power has reached safety limit allowed for scan parameters and patient weight. Check patient weight entered.

entries.extended_error: The SCP board battery is low. This board is located in the System Cabinet, MGD Chassis, front slot 12. If the system loses power, it may not be possible to reboot the system. The SCP board should be replaced. In the event that the battery has failed, the customer system will not boot, and no replacement SCP board is immediately available, you can work around this problem by moving SCP jumper J32 from position 1-2 to position 2-3. This should allow the system to boot and scan, but it disables the SCP power-on diagnostics. A replacement SCP board should be installed as soon as possible.

entries.extended_error:
The board may be in one of the following states:
0 - No response, 1 - OS Loaded, 2 - PPC Bug, 3 - PPC Diag, 4 - OS not loaded
If the error message states that the board is in state 4, then the OS load was stopped. This may happen if characters are detected on the serial cable. In order to eliminate this problem, disconnect the serial cable from AGP/COM1 Connector or SCP/Console Connector and reboot the board. If the error message states that the board is in state 2 or 3, then run the Motorola Board Level Diagnostics to verify the board is OK. If the BLD passes but this message appears during TPS reset then it is highly probable that the boards are not being reset by STIF(or PSE) connection. You can verify if the boards are not being reset by STIF(or PSE) connection during TPS reset either by looking at the LEDs on front of the boards or by opening MGD Terminal window.

entries.extended_error:
This fault was detected by the Driver Module. An open circuit fault occurs when the actual value is less than the pre-defined limit. Check system cables, connectors, coils and configurations. Re-seat all coil connectors. The mask of all failed channels indicates additional channels with the same fault - convert the hex number to a bitmap to decipher the mask, with channel 1 indicated by the least significant bit and channel 16 indicated by the most significant bit. For example, a mask of 0x3c converts to 0011 1100, meaning channels 3, 4, 5, and 6 all experienced the same failure. The key at the bottom of the error message shows the MC driver bias channels provided by the Driver Module used with each multicoil connector. Note that some systems may not have all the connectors listed. Tools such as Gather Load Data located on the CSD Diagnostics page under Peripherals, Driver Module Diagnostics can help with isolating this failure to a coil, cable, LPCA module, or Driver Module.
In 20.0 and later systems, MC bias is supplied and sensed by the RF Hub, so this message should not be logged. TPS reset may help recover.

entries.message:
Bridge Datapath Diagnostic - Doorbell Interrupt test failed when the master processor failed to acknowledge the interrupt was cleared by the slave processor.
Master Proc = %s
Slave Proc = %s Doorbells = 0x%08x
Poll Attempts = %d
entries.extended_error:
The interrupt was issued to the slave processor side of the Bridge module. An ISR on the slave processor should have been called when the doorbell was issued and then detected by the slave processor. The ISR clears the corresponding doorbell interrupt. Meanwhile, the master processor is polling the doorbell interrupt's status bit, checking for a cleared interrupt. After several polling attempts, the master processor failed to detect the interrupt was cleared, resulting in an error. Fault isolation is as follows:
Using a bus analyzer, verify the interrupt was issued by the master processor to the slave processor's doorbell on the Bridge module. Using a bus analyzer on the slave side of the Bridge module, verify the doorbell asserted an interrupt on the slave-side PCI bus. Also, verify the slave processor cleared the interrupt. Lastly, verify the master processor repeatedly polled the Bridge module for the cleared interrupt bit. A failure at any point will assist in fault generation (processor, communications/connectivity, or Bridge).

Master Proc = %s
Slave Proc = %s
Function = %s
Poll Attempts = %d.
entries.extended_error:
Requests to execute functions on the slave processor are initiated by the master processor using a 'slave command' interface. When called, an interface function that initiates remote execution only verifies that the function exists on the slave processor and that it can be executed. Provided those conditions are satisfied, execution of the function on the slave processor begins. The master processor verifies the function on the slave processor is done by polling the interface. This error is generated after several polling attempts failed to verify the issued command completed execution on the slave processor. Possible causes (1) issued command is still running, (2) issued command is in an endless loop,
(3) race conditions within the interface due to multiple commands being issued, or (4) problem with interface used to issued commands to the slave processor.

You can isolate the effect of the STIF(or PSEIO) board by removing that board (power down first) and running the SRF(or PSE)-IRF(or IXG) diag again. The system will not run without the STIF(or PSEIO) board but the SRF(or PSE)-IRF(or IXG) diag can be run. If the test passes without the STIF(or PSEIO) the STIF(or PSEIO) is defective. Otherwise, the problem is in the SRF(or PSE), IRF(or IXG), or backplane. Check for bent packplane pins. Re-seating the IRF(or IXG)/SRF(or PSE)/STIF(or PSEIO) might help.

entries.extended_error: The SAR limits are adjusted based on the temperature read by the scan room temperature sensor. For each degree above 23.5 degrees C, the SAR limit is reduced by 0.25. If the predicted SAR of a given scan is expected to exceed the SAR limit imposed by the scan room ambient temperature, the scan will be inhibited. The most likely cause of this error is the scan room air conditioning not being set to a low enough temperature. This could also be caused by a faulty scan room air temperature sensor.

entries.extended_error: This is most likely a problem with a 80MHz reference clock signal to one or more external modules. entries.extended_error: When the TDM detects noise in the scan room larger than the preset threshold value, the TDM commands the receivers to ignore the analog input signals and just send zeros in their digital outputs. This reduces the impact of a noise spike on the output image but still degrades the image somewhat. This error message indicates that the system detected an unusually large amount of noise during the previous scan. Check the scan room door seals and for other sources of noise inside the scan room such as: loose metal on metal contact of fasteners and hardware, incandescent bulbs with noisy filaments, fluorescent lighting, and 3rd-party electronic devices. Use the EPI White Pixel Test or Spike Noise Triangulation tool to locate the noise sources.

entries.message:
AGP detected a fault on the fiber links connected to IRF3 or IXG or ERF.
The link to this device dropped out: %s
entries.extended_error: A momentary problem with any module connected to the DVMR dual fiber links can bring the links down for every node. The IRF3 can detect which link was the first to drop out. The module connected to that link should be the one who initiated the problem. If several modules dropped out at the same time the IRF3 will report multiple modules. In this case there might be a single problem effecting multiple modules such as a power supply glitch or a drop out on the shared reference clock source. Note: a problem on the RRX to ICN links will cause the RRX to IRF3 link to go down so errors reported against the RRX may be caused by a problem with an ICN.

entries.message: An error on the XGD has prevented TPS reset from completing successfully. Please review the log for XGD faults to determine the cause and action(s) to take. Perform another TPS reset and if this error occurs again, contact your service representative.
entries.extended_error:
If no XGD specific faults are available, try the following steps:
* Verify that the 420 volt circuit breaker on the PDU is on.
* Verify that the DVMR link fiberoptic cable form the IRF3(or IXG) is connected to the GMC DVMR link transceiver in XGD.
* Verify that the IRF3(or IXG) and GMC DVMR link transeivers are operational.
* Verify that the DVMR link cable from IRF3(or IXG) to the GMC is not damaged.
* Verify that the transeiver from the exciter to the GMC clock input is good.
* Verify that the clock fiberoptic cable form the exiter to the GMC is good.
* Power down the XGD and verify that the GMC, XGA-CB and XPS-CB boards are seated securely in their slots by removing and re-seating each board. Power on the XGD and perform a TPS reset.
* Power down the MGD chassis and verify that IRF3(or IXG) is seated securely in its slot by removing and re-seating it. Power on the MGD chassis and perform a TPS reset.

entries.message:
The RF Hub detected an error searching for devices on the HART ID bus.
Error: %d
entries.extended_error:
Check the HART ID cable connected to the reroute box and the body coil. The one-wire search error will not impact ability to perform clinical scans.
Systems with an RFSBv or RFSB2 switch board in RF Hub Slots 1 (and 2, in case of 32 ch systems), will not have a Reroute Box. In such systems, this message is applicable to the devices which connected to the same one-wire bus. The Reroute box (if present), Preamp Combiner (if present), DTRSW (if present) and Body coil HART ID devices share a single one-wire bus controlled by the RF Hub. This error message is logged when the one-wire bus is shorted or when an invalid HART ID is received by the RF Hub. Check for bent pins at each connector in this path and test for one-wire bus short circuits within the cables. Refer to the system cabling diagrams. Run the RF Hub Board Level Diagnostic to retry the HART ID search.

entries.extended_error:
A bias drive fault was detected by the RF Hub. This happens when the RF Hub tries to drive a multicoil bias voltage, but detects that the voltage driven is outside of the expected range.
Ignore this error if there are also RF Hub power failures reported. If no power failures are reported, this is likely a faulty RF Hub RFCB or MCDB.
Run the Multicoil Bias Diagnostic or Coil Datapath Diagnostic to troubleshoot.
Explanation of fields:
Connector - The coil connector the fault was detected on. Fault bitmap - This is a hexadecimal bit map of all the faulted channels. For example, 0x3 means faults on channels 1 and 2. 0x80000000 means channel 32. Used bitmap - This is a hexadecimal bit map of the channels on this connector that are known to be connected to a coil. First channel - The first channel that faulted, and the number of channels on the connector. Driven - The voltage programmed. Read - The voltage read back that is outside of the expected range.
